question: Will the winner of Alaska's 2026 gubernatorial election receive fewer votes in the first round than another candidate?

calls.reasoning: YES requires a come-from-behind RCV win. Kreiss-Tomkins (D) leads first-choice polling 40-50% vs Wilson ~20-30%, with Bronson and Taylor splitting the rest, so if he wins he almost certainly led round one (NO). YES ≈ P(Republican wins) × ~0.9. Prediction markets put a Republican win around 13-22% (Kalshi ~13% Wilson via aggregator; Polymarket figures reported ~21-22%, one stale/conflicting 42%). Counter: an Alaska Survey Research poll found ~18% undecided who lean strongly right; GOP first-choice total is near 50%, so consolidation behind Wilson in later rounds is possible.
calls.dossier:
- Election Nov 3, 2026; RCV general with 4 tickets: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), Bernadette Wilson (R), Dave Bronson (R), Treg Taylor (R) (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-10-25).
- Aug 18 primary: Kreiss-Tomkins 22.5%, Tom Begich (D) 20.8%, Wilson 10.0%, Bronson 8.1%, Taylor 7.3% (5th; advanced after Begich withdrew). Begich later endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins (Wikipedia; prediction.com Sep 19).
- Alaska Survey Research Oct 15-18 first choice: KT 50, Wilson 30, Bronson 12, Taylor 8 (Wikipedia/270toWin).
- Data for Progress Oct 8-16: KT 46, Wilson 28, Bronson 12, Taylor 9.
- NYT/Siena Sep 24-Oct 1: KT 40, Wilson 20, Bronson 15, Taylor 11.
- ASR Oct 1-3 final RCV round: KT 54, Wilson 46. RCP two-way average KT +7.4 (3 polls).
- ASR Sept poll (Alaska Public, 2026-09-22): KT 40% first round, wins final by 10; ~18% undecided, who lean right (Trump +30 among them per pollster Bob Ward).
- Markets: Kalshi and Polymarket price the winner; contract differs from this question (winner vs. first-round trailing winner). Prices are in run reasoning, not here.
- Status quo: the first-round leader wins. YES only occurs if a Republican overtakes KT after transfers (or, implausibly, KT wins without leading round one).
- Resolves off official Alaska Division of Elections first-choice counts for the winner vs. any other candidate.
- Event window: general election Nov 3, 2026 -> official results; as of 2026-10-25 voting not complete.
- Searched for but not found: direct Kalshi page data (rate-limited), any market on first-round-vs-winner specifically.
calls.reference_class: RCV/IRV elections where the first-round leader has a double-digit lead; comeback wins are rare (~5-10% of multi-round races overall), conditioned here on the market-implied chance of an upset

calls.reasoning: Kreiss-Tomkins (D) leads every poll on first choices by 12-30 points (40-50% vs Wilson's 20-30%). So he cannot win without also topping round one, and YES effectively means 'a Republican wins after vote transfers'. Under ranked-choice voting, the final-round polls give KT 52-55% to Wilson's 45-48%, roughly a 7-point margin across 5 polls. Prediction markets give Wilson about 13-22% (Kalshi about 86% KT; Polymarket about 79% KT per a search snippet, plus one possibly stale Polymarket US snippet showing Wilson ahead). Those markets ask who wins outright, which is nearly equivalent to this question here. Cook reportedly rates the race a toss-up. In Alaska, 7-point poll leads have sometimes been beaten by polling error, and ballots that exhaust before the final round add uncertainty. I land around 20%.
calls.dossier:
- Candidates in the general (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-10-25): Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), Bernadette Wilson (R), Dave Bronson (R), Treg Taylor (R). Tom Begich (D) finished 2nd in the 2026-08-18 primary with 20.8% but withdrew and endorsed KT; Taylor, who was 5th with 7.3%, advanced. Primary: KT 22.5%, Wilson 10.0%, Bronson 8.1%.
- First-choice polls (Wikipedia): ASR Oct 15-18 KT 50/Wilson 30/Bronson 12/Taylor 8; DFP Oct 8-16 46/28/12/9; ASR Oct 1-3 48/27/15/10; NYT/Siena Sep 24-Oct 1 40/20/15/11; Cygnal Sep 24-27 44/24/8/9; co/efficient Sep 14-17 43/20/17/6; Fabrizio Sep 8-11 40/20/14/7.
- Final-round polls, KT vs Wilson: ASR Oct 15-18 55-45; DFP 53-47 (MoE ±4); ASR Oct 1-3 54-46; NYT/Siena 52-48; Fabrizio 55-45. RCP two-way average KT +7.4 (3 polls).
- Cook Political Report reportedly moved the race to toss-up (The Hill; date not confirmed).
- Combined Republican first-choice share in polls is about 46-55%. Ballots from Bronson and Taylor voters that don't rank Wilson exhaust and do not transfer.
- Structure: KT leads first choices by 12-30 points in every poll. So YES requires a Republican (in practice Wilson) to win after transfers while trailing in round one; a KT win resolves NO.
- Markets: Kalshi and Polymarket both list winner markets (prices kept out of this dossier). One Polymarket US snippet disagreed with the others and may be stale.
- Election day is 2026-11-03 per news. Alaska tabulates RCV after absentee ballots arrive, about 2 weeks later; resolution follows official results.
- Resolves off official first-choice vote counts vs the eventual winner, not off polls.
- Searched for but not found: post-Oct-20 polls, verified current market prices, the date of the Cook toss-up rating.
calls.reference_class: Statewide races where the poll leader on first choices also leads final-round polls by about 5-8 points one week out; the trailing side wins about 15-25% of the time

calls.reasoning: Kreiss-Tomkins (sole D) leads first-choice polling 40-50% vs Wilson 20-30%, so Yes ≈ P(a Republican wins via RCV transfers). Final-round polls show KT +6 to +8 (DfP 53-47, ASR 54-46); Polymarket ~22% Wilson; Cook moved to Toss Up while others Lean/Solid D. Small upward adjustment for Alaska polling error and possible R consolidation; essentially zero chance KT wins without leading round one.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia (accessed 2026-10-25): general-election ballot is Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), Bernadette Wilson (R), Dave Bronson (R), Treg Taylor (R). Aug 18 primary: Kreiss-Tomkins 22.5%, Tom Begich (D) 20.8% (withdrew and endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins), Wilson 10.0%, Bronson 8.1%, Taylor 7.3% (moved into the top four after Begich withdrew).
- Data for Progress poll, Oct 8-16 2026, 694 likely voters, MoE ±4: first choice Kreiss-Tomkins 46, Wilson 28, Bronson 12, Taylor 9; final RCV round Kreiss-Tomkins 53, Wilson 47. DfP notes that if exhausted Republican-ranked ballots had all transferred to Wilson, the race could tie.
- Alaska Survey Research poll, Oct 15-18 (per Wikipedia and Political Wire, 2026-10-20): first choice Kreiss-Tomkins 50, Wilson 30, Bronson 12, Taylor 8; head-to-head 54-46 Kreiss-Tomkins.
- NYT/Siena poll (reported via search snippet, date unclear): first choice Kreiss-Tomkins 40, Wilson 20, Bronson 15, Taylor 11; the gap narrows a lot in the RCV tally.
- RealClearPolling average of two-way polls (search snippet): Kreiss-Tomkins 53.7, Wilson 46.3 across 3 polls.
- Cook Political Report moved the race from Lean R to Toss Up (The Hill, date unclear); Wikipedia lists late-October ratings of Lean D or Solid D from multiple forecasters.
- ADN, 2026-09-04: Wilson urged Republicans not to 'rank the red' and asked Bronson and Taylor to drop out; Bronson and Taylor released a joint video urging Republicans to rank all three Republicans.
- Structural note: with the sole Democrat leading first choices by roughly 15-25 points, a Republican winner would almost certainly have trailed in round one; a Kreiss-Tomkins win would almost certainly come with a round-one lead. The question therefore effectively reduces to whether a Republican wins after RCV transfers.
- Status quo: Kreiss-Tomkins leads the first round and the final-round polls.
- Resolves off official certified results (Alaska Division of Elections); RCV tabulation is typically released about two weeks after Election Day.
- Event window: the Nov 3 2026 general election through official results; as of 2026-10-25 voting has not concluded.
- Searched but could not get: the live Kalshi price (page returned HTTP 429); the full Cook article (HTTP 403).
calls.reference_class: Alaska RCV statewide races where one party's candidate leads first round by 15+ pts but the opposing party is split; leaders with modest final-round poll leads ~1 week out

calls.reasoning: YES requires a Republican (in practice Wilson) to win via RCV transfers while trailing Kreiss-Tomkins in round one; a KT win is NO since he leads first choices by 12-30 points in every poll. Final-round polls show KT +6 to +10 across five pollsters (ASR 55-45, DfP 53-47, NYT/Siena 52-48). Markets reportedly price a Republican win around 13-22%. Wilson's discouraging of ranking other Republicans raises exhaustion and hurts consolidation. Allowance for Alaska polling error and right-leaning undecideds keeps it near one in five.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on how the question works (YES is close to P(Republican wins)) and on the poll numbers. Their spread (0.17-0.23) comes from how much each added for polling error and for Cook's reported toss-up rating. Market prices (Kalshi ~86% KT, Polymarket ~78-79%) could not be checked live because there is no web access on this run; they stay as approximate evidence pointing to a 13-22% Republican win. The Cook rating is undated and conflicts with the late-October Lean/Solid D ratings listed on Wikipedia, so I gave it little weight. Taking the markets, the late ratings, and the exhaustion dynamics from Wilson's anti-'rank the red' message together, I land at 0.18.

disagreements.claim: Size of the uplift for Alaska polling error and right-leaning undecideds
disagreements.verdict: A moderate uplift above the market midpoint is not warranted, given that exhaustion works against Wilson; 0.18
